A janitor approaches, mop in hand, and asks if someone in the photo is known to him. Mike replies that it's him, lost in the memory. The janitor studies the image and remarks on how cruel adolescence can be. Mike insists he had everything in that moment—confidence, possibility—before it all vanished. The janitor recites a line about the sadness of 'what might have been.' Mike says it would make a fitting epitaph. The janitor replies that everyone has regrets, and though things may seem fixed, it can't hurt to ask, to wonder what might still be possible. Mike looks at the janitor, about to ask how he knew his name, when his children appear down the hall, calling out. He turns back—the janitor is gone. Mike greets his kids, apologizes for being late, and they head toward the door, Mike limping as they walk.

name: Mike Confronts Ed Over the Samples Case
description: Ed cowers against the back wall, clutching an oversized loofah with both hands. The door creaks open and Mike steps inside, eyes narrowing. He sees Ed’s panicked stance and laughs. Ed gasps, holding the loofah out like a shield. Mike takes a step forward. 'Don’t come any closer! I’ll use it!' Ed shouts. Mike smirks. 'What are you gonna do? Exfoliate me to death?' Ed whimpers, pointing a trembling finger at the mirror. Mike glances over, then back at Ed. 'You got into my samples case again, didn’t you?' Ed doesn’t answer. Mike’s voice grows sharper. 'What’s your problem? It’s only mud.' The muddy feet in the mirror shift slightly. Mike freezes. His face drains of color. 'AAAAAAAHHHHHHH!!!' He stumbles to the sink, turns the faucet, and splashes water on his face. The mud washes away, but his reflection remains that of a 17-year-old. He screams again. Frantically, he tears off his jacket and shirt, then yanks down his pants, peering into his boxers. Still screaming, he grabs Ed by the robe. 'Do something! Anything! Pinch me!' Ed drives his knee into Mike’s groin, then sprints for the door, shrieking. Mike collapses to the floor, groaning. 'I said pinch!'

Ed listens with amusement, admitting he saw the video on YouTube and found it funny. Mike says he won’t go back to the school. Ed urges him to take control, to dominate the students, but Mike insists he can’t do it. The bartender approaches, and Mike orders a double scotch neat, but Ed intervenes, ordering a Shirley Temple with extra cherries instead. Mike corrects the name and greets her. Ms. Goodwin invites them to sit. Ed immediately declares that Mike is a bastard because he was born out of wedlock, then adds that he is single and wealthy. Mike interjects, explaining that his mother is a successful prostitute from Thailand. Ed falls silent. Ms. Goodwin, visibly taken aback, asks for Mike’s transcripts. He hands over a folder, and as she reviews his academic record from Cutler High in Connecticut, Ed and Mike begin playfully fighting—pinching and elbowing each other. They stop when she looks up. Ms. Goodwin comments on Mike’s strong grades. Ed claims credit for helping with homework. Mike then says, 'Dad, the doctor called. You were right. It is herpes.' Ed stares in shock. Ms. Goodwin stands and calls for Lisa, an 18-year-old staff member, who enters. She asks Lisa to print a schedule and take Mike to class. Lisa leads Mike out. Ed tells him to behave and sit up straight. After Mike leaves, Ed turns to Ms. Goodwin and says, 'They grow up so fast. Mojito?' She asks what he means. He suggests a Cuban place with good plantains, implying a date. She declines, stating she doesn’t date parents. Ed threatens to enroll Mike elsewhere. She says she needs to get back to work and ushers him to the door. As she closes it, Ed calls out, 'See you at the next bake sale then?' Ms. Goodwin shakes her head in disbelief.
